source.title: Cascading effects of bird functional extinction reduce pollination and plant density

design: North Island mainland sites with depleted native bird pollinators compared with three nearby offshore bird-sanctuary islands retaining native bird assemblages.

source_native_anchors.demographic_result: juvenile-to-adult abundance was lower where bird pollination function was depleted

observed_chain: native bird functional loss -> stronger pollen limitation -> lower seed production -> lower plant recruitment/density
why_admitted: the pollinator-functional contrast is externally imposed by bird-community loss rather than fitted to the ABM
pollination and downstream reproductive outcomes change in the same direction
the system is geographically independent of the six-system frozen harness
no ABM parameter is retuned to the source
claim_boundary: This is a strong qualitative propagation test, not a numerical fit of the ABM and not a source-native mapping of the specific synthetic trait-position mechanism. The island-refuge comparison also bundles other mainland-island ecological differences, so the source's natural-experiment interpretation is retained without converting it into a universal causal coefficient.
